note: Every entry was checked against a bibliographic registry on verified_on. Numbers quoted in the cards are traceable to the 'used_for' field. No entry is taken from the restricted ABY manual.

references.title: Interpreting results of ethanol analysis in postmortem specimens: a review of the literature
references.used_for: Postmortem specimens (vitreous humor, urine, bile, bone marrow, intracranial clot), microbial synthesis, postmortem diffusion, bodies from water, water-content of autopsy blood, non-oxidative ethanol markers.
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP lookup_article_by_citation + get_article_metadata; NCBI E-utilities esummary (print/epub dates)

references.title: Ethanol analysis by headspace gas chromatography with simultaneous flame-ionization and mass spectrometry detection
references.used_for: Headspace GC with simultaneous FID quantitation and MS confirmation (Dean's switch); validation concept (calibration, precision, accuracy).

references.title: Biochemical pathways generating post-mortem volatile compounds co-detected during forensic ethanol analyses
references.used_for: Microbial fermentation of carbohydrates, amino acids, glycerol and fatty acids after death; co-detected volatiles (incl. 1-propanol, acetaldehyde, acetone); relevance for internal-standard selection.
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP lookup_article_by_citation + get_article_metadata; NCBI E-utilities esummary

references.title: Evaluation and review of ways to differentiate sources of ethanol in postmortem blood
references.used_for: Distinguishing ingested vs postmortem-produced ethanol: alternative specimens, EtG/EtS, 5-HTOL/5-HIAA, n-propanol and n-butanol as putrefaction markers; Candida species.

references.title: Preanalytical factors influencing the stability of ethanol in antemortem blood and urine samples
references.used_for: Storage stability, sodium fluoride preservative, tendency of BAC to decrease on storage, in-vitro ethanol synthesis in urine with glycosuria/infection without NaF.

references.title: A comparison between the enzymatic oxidation method and headspace gas chromatography with a flame ionization detector in the determination of postmortem blood ethanol
references.used_for: Lactate and LDH in postmortem blood interfere with the enzymatic oxidation method (positive bias); authors recommend HS-GC-FID for postmortem blood.

references.title: Comparison of hospital laboratory serum alcohol levels obtained by an enzymatic method with whole blood levels forensically determined by gas chromatography
references.used_for: Serum (enzymatic) vs whole blood (HS-GC) ethanol: the serum/whole-blood ratio is concentration-dependent, so no single conversion factor applies.

references.title: Reflections on variability in the blood-breath ratio of ethanol and its importance when evidential breath-alcohol instruments are used in law enforcement
references.used_for: Breath alcohol as a surrogate of BAC; blood/breath ratio depends on analytical, sampling and physiological factors (breath and body temperature, exhalation time, absorption phase).
references.verified_via: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esummary + efetch abstract); Crossref API works/{doi}

references.title: Evidence-based survey of the elimination rates of ethanol from blood with applications in forensic casework
references.used_for: Inter-individual variation of ethanol elimination rate; caution for back-calculation (qualitative only in the card).
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP get_article_metadata; NCBI E-utilities esummary

references.title: Concentration units used to report blood- and breath-alcohol concentration for legal purposes differ between countries which is important to consider when blood/breath ratios of alcohol are compared and contrasted
references.used_for: Reporting units for blood/breath alcohol differ between countries (qualitative).

references.title: Alternative determination of blood alcohol concentration by (1)H NMR spectroscopy
references.journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Analysis
references.used_for: 1H NMR proposed as an alternative quantitative method, compared against ADH and HS-GC reference methods.
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP get_article_metadata; NCBI E-utilities esummary

references.title: Drowning: still a difficult autopsy diagnosis
references.used_for: No single definitive test for drowning; diatom test combined with autopsy findings; biological and thanato-chemical adjunct methods.
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP lookup_article_by_citation + get_article_metadata; NCBI E-utilities esummary

references.title: Scanning and transmission electron microscopical evidence of the capacity of diatoms to penetrate the alveolo-capillary barrier in drowning
references.used_for: Experimental (rat) SEM/TEM evidence that diatoms can cross the alveolo-capillary barrier during drowning.

references.title: Diatoms and homicide
references.used_for: Femoral bone marrow as sample; comparison with water from the putative drowning medium; usefulness in decomposed and burned bodies; maxillary sinus fluid.

references.title: Diatoms and drowning--a review
references.used_for: Classical review of the diatom test (historical context).

references.title: Diatom detection in the diagnosis of death by drowning
references.used_for: Contamination-free sampling at the start of autopsy; water samples from surface and bed of the site; quantitative, qualitative and morphological recording; similarity indices; interdisciplinary (algological) interpretation.

references.title: Objective diagnosis of drowning by the "diatom test" - a critical review
references.note: No DOI is registered in PubMed for this article; none is given.
references.used_for: Contamination as main source of false positives; passive postmortem penetration into lungs; bone marrow preferred; acid/oxidative vs enzymatic digestion; light microscopy screening with SEM/ESEM confirmation.

references.title: The medico-legal interpretation of diatom findings for the diagnosis of fatal drowning: a systematic review
references.used_for: Systematic review: evidentiary value uncertain, poor comparability between studies, unclear significance of false positives/negatives, antemortem and postmortem contamination, need for standardization and diatomologist collaboration.

references.title: Diatom analysis in drowning: a critical review of reliability, contamination, and medico-legal interpretation
references.used_for: Vulnerability of low-count findings in closed organs to contamination; DNA-based/metagenomic approaches; proposition-based interpretation and reporting.

references.title: Mathematical contributions to the theory of evolution. V. On the reconstruction of the stature of prehistoric races
references.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A
references.note: Not indexed in PubMed. Crossref deposits '192' in the issue field; the journal's numbering treats it as volume 192.
references.used_for: Historical foundation of regression-based stature reconstruction.

references.title: Estimation of stature from long bones of American Whites and Negroes
references.note: Title reproduced as published in 1952 (historical terminology).
references.used_for: Classical sex- and group-specific regression equations.

references.title: A re-evaluation of estimation of stature based on measurements of stature taken during life and of long bones after death
references.used_for: Re-evaluation using statures measured during life.

references.title: The measure and mismeasure of the tibia: implications for stature estimation
references.used_for: Trotter omitted the malleolus when measuring the tibia; her tibia measurements were 10-12 mm short and, applied to properly measured tibiae, the formulae overestimate stature on average by 2.5-3.0 cm (abstract).
references.verified_via: PubMed MCP lookup_article_by_citation + get_article_metadata (PMID, abstract); Crossref API bibliographic query (DOI)

references.title: Measuring the tibia: Trotter's error revisited
references.used_for: Confirms that the malleolus adjustment for Trotter's tibia remains valid.

references.title: Secular change in long bone length and proportion in the United States, 1800-1970
references.used_for: Secular change in long-bone length and proportions; stronger in males, lower limb and distal bones.

references.title: Secular changes in the postcranial skeleton of American Whites
references.used_for: Positive secular change in all long-bone lengths and stature; changing limb proportions.

references.title: Stature estimation and calibration: Bayesian and maximum likelihood perspectives in physical anthropology
references.used_for: Inverse vs classical calibration; inverse preferred when the reference sample is a reasonable prior, classical when extrapolating beyond the reference sample.

references.title: Evaluation of stature estimation from the database for forensic anthropology
references.used_for: Trotter-Gleser equations not appropriate for the modern forensic context; equations based on forensic (reported) stature and modern samples.

references.title: A method for assessment of maximum long bone length and living stature from fragmentary long bones

references.title: Stature estimation equations for modern American Indians in the American Southwest
